summary: Jyh-Jing Hwang opens with a history of autonomous driving from simple 1980s neural networks to NVIDIA's early end-to-end driving models (~2020) and Waymo's current L4 system, which uses separate perception, prediction, and planning modules. Waymo operates rider-only services in Phoenix, San Francisco, Austin, and LA, expanding to approximately ten cities including Tokyo, creating pressure to solve long-tail driving scenarios at scale. Gemini demonstrates strong generalization on rare events like construction zones, flocks of birds, and scooter accidents, motivating EMMA (End-to-End Multimodal Model for Autonomous Driving). EMMA takes routing text and eight 360-degree camera video inputs, feeds them to Gemini, and outputs future waypoints. It is self-supervised from driving logs, camera-only, and HD-map-free. EMMA achieves state-of-the-art on NuScenes. Adding chain-of-thought reasoning—identifying critical objects, explaining behavior, and stating meta-decisions—improves results further, surpassing specialized baselines (Wayformer, MotionLM) on Waymo's Open Motion Dataset (~100k scenes). Scaling laws hold: more training data continues reducing perplexity and improving planning. EMMA extends to multi-task training including 3D detection, road graph estimation, and free-form VQA. The talk then addresses evaluation: open-loop replay is insufficient, so Waymo explores simulation and real-world testing. Simulation is trusted more than open-loop evaluation. The Drive&Gen research approach uses open-sourced generative video models from Google (including Veo 2 from DeepMind) for sensor simulation, creating realistic synthetic videos to test EMMA's planner under controlled conditions—changing weather, time of day, and other environmental factors. Results align with intuition: rain degrades the camera-only planner, nighttime is worse than daytime, and the model performs best at noon or afternoon. Hwang highlights that Waymo's Alphabet affiliation grants access to Google's foundation models, enabling ongoing research to improve generalization and scale autonomous driving.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.
temporalContext: Transcript claims reflect the publication date; linked external context was checked at the run's research date.
takeaways: EMMA is an end-to-end multimodal autonomous driving model built on Gemini that processes camera video and routing text to directly output driving waypoints.
Chain-of-thought reasoning—identifying critical objects, explaining their behavior, and stating meta-decisions before planning—improves planner performance and adds explainability.
EMMA achieves state-of-the-art on NuScenes and outperforms specialized baselines (Wayformer, MotionLM) on Waymo's Open Motion Dataset (~100k scenes, ~100x larger than NuScenes).
Multi-task co-training spans trajectory planning, 3D detection, road graph estimation, and free-form VQA, with detection quality comparable to dedicated state-of-the-art models.
Foundation models like Gemini generalize well to rare long-tail driving events, which are critical for scaling autonomous driving across cities.
Open-loop evaluation is insufficient for faithful validation; simulation and real-world testing are more trusted approaches.
Drive&Gen uses generative video models from Google (e.g., Veo 2) for sensor simulation, enabling controlled evaluation under varied weather, time-of-day, and environmental conditions.
Simulation results confirm expected degradation patterns: rain and nighttime degrade the camera-only EMMA planner, with best performance at noon/afternoon.
Waymo's Alphabet affiliation provides access to Google's foundation models for free, enabling ongoing research to improve generalization and scaling.
Understand Waymo's autonomous driving system architecture and its perception-prediction-planning pipeline

sections.title: History and Current State of Autonomous Driving
sections.summary: Hwang traces autonomous driving from 1980s neural networks to NVIDIA's early end-to-end models (~2020) and contrasts them with Waymo's L4 system, which uses perception, prediction, and planning to safely drive in San Francisco.

sections.title: Scaling Challenges and Long-Tail Events
sections.summary: Waymo operates in four cities and is expanding to about ten including Tokyo. Long-tail scenarios like construction zones with conflicting traffic signals are rare for individuals but common at Waymo's scale, motivating more generalizable solutions.

sections.title: Foundation Model Generalization with Gemini
sections.summary: Gemini demonstrates strong generalization on rare events such as flocks of birds and scooter accidents, correctly identifying scenarios and recommending appropriate driving responses.

sections.title: EMMA Architecture and Core Traits
sections.summary: EMMA feeds routing text and eight-camera video into Gemini to output future waypoints. It is self-supervised, camera-only, and HD-map-free, achieving state-of-the-art on NuScenes.

sections.title: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning and Stronger Baselines
sections.summary: Adding chain-of-thought reasoning—identifying critical objects, explaining behaviors, and stating meta-decisions—improves planner quality. On Waymo's Open Motion Dataset (~100k scenes), EMMA surpasses specialized baselines like Wayformer and MotionLM. Scaling laws show continued improvement with more data.

sections.title: Multi-Task Co-Training and Evaluation Challenge
sections.summary: EMMA extends to 3D detection, road graph estimation, and free-form VQA with detection quality comparable to state-of-the-art. The talk raises open-loop versus closed-loop evaluation as the next critical challenge for validating end-to-end models.

sections.title: Drive&Gen: Sensor Simulation for End-to-End Evaluation
sections.summary: Open-loop replay is insufficient for faithful evaluation; simulation and real-world testing are more trusted. Waymo's Drive&Gen approach uses open-sourced generative video models from Google (including Veo 2 from DeepMind) to create realistic sensor simulation videos for testing EMMA under controlled conditions—varying weather, time of day, and other factors. Results confirm expected patterns: rain degrades the camera-only planner, nighttime is worse than daytime, and best performance occurs at noon or afternoon. Hwang notes Waymo's Alphabet affiliation enables access to Google's foundation models for ongoing research toward improved generalization and scaling.
